body.estimand_functional: \(F_{\mathcal J}(f,q)=\min_{b\in\mathcal E_{\mathcal J}:b\ge f}\mathbb E_q[b]=\max_{\mu:\mu|_{O_z}=q|_{O_z}\;\forall z}\mathbb E_\mu[f]\)

sampling_model.design: A known finite randomization \(p\) on its support \(Z\) is the only source of randomness; its support probabilities may be arbitrary positive real numbers.
sampling_model.treatment: Assignment \(z\) reveals exactly \(\theta|_{O_z}\) and the score is \(X_z=v_z^\top\theta\).
sampling_model.overlap: The set \(Z\) is the support of \(p\); a monomial is implementable only when \(\pi_S>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None in the finite characterization; the triangular-array result separately assumes a design-based law of large numbers for the chosen bound implementation.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Quadratic-form estimability is equivalent to pairwise design compatibility, and positive-definite targeted matrix objectives characterize the admissible quadratic bounds.
Arbitrary design--linear-estimator--variance-bound triplets are represented and estimated through quadratic matrix bounds.
Binary inclusion--exclusion yields a sharp variance improvement for a \(2^2\) factorial design.
Observed marginal distributions yield asymptotically sharp variance bounds for the difference-in-means estimator under complete randomization.
Proposition 2 and Corollary 2 give a weakly conservative Horvitz--Thompson variance correction when pairwise inclusion probabilities are zero.
Inverse-probability exposure estimators admit conservative randomization variance estimators and local-dependence asymptotics.
Finite-population central limit theorems justify randomization-based causal-effect inference for several structured designs.
Imputation and contrast constructions give conservative variance estimators for broad randomized designs and recover Neyman's estimator in standard cases.
Under random binary potential outcomes and balanced designs, CMH- and Robins-type estimators are conservative and can be asymptotically tight.

body.tldr: A six-coordinate three-atom experiment has an exactly certified nonnegative quartic variance-bound optimum \(107/72\), whereas every observable quadratic or cubic bound, including every published Harshaw--Middleton--Savje quadratic candidate, is at least \(55/36\); the exact separation is \(1/24\). For fixed binary potential outcomes under any finite known randomization with arbitrary real probabilities on its support, expected observed-data rules are exactly the Boolean Mobius span generated by jointly observable coordinate subsets, universal conservativeness is finite pointwise domination, and an observable-margin dual characterizes the full Pareto-admissible class. Proposal-specific complement symmetry explains the quartic threshold, independent replication preserves the block gap, and conservative studentized inference is conditional on blockwise conservativeness and a denominator law of large numbers.

project_justification.gap: The closest arbitrary-design theory, \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026}, explicitly restricts the candidate bounds to quadratic forms. The zero-pairwise-inclusion correction of \cite{AronowSamii2013} supplies a conservative Horvitz--Thompson rule but not the full observable-function cone or its Pareto frontier; the binary sharp-bound papers \cite{Lu2019FactorialBinary} and \cite{AronowGreenLee2014} treat special designs and different observable information.
project_justification.niche: Binary support makes every expected observed-data rule a finite multilinear function, so assignment-specific higher-order observability can be characterized without stochastic outcome assumptions.
project_justification.fill: The project leads with the exact \(107/72\) versus \(55/36\) quartic separation, then gives the if-and-only-if Boolean support theorem, pointwise conservative cone, observable-margin dual, Pareto complete class for real support probabilities, rational certificate corollary, product law, nonnegative implementation, and a bounded independent-block studentization theorem.

body.related_work: \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026}, especially Proposition 1, Theorems 1 and 3, Definitions 1--2, and Section 8, supplies the quadratic characterization and supporting-objective techniques and explicitly leaves larger bound classes open. The pairwise design-compatibility criterion implies that every published Harshaw--Middleton--Savje quadratic candidate belongs to the Boolean quadratic and cubic comparison cone used by the exact lower certificate; this inclusion is strict because the Boolean cone permits intercepts and requires domination only on \(\Theta\), whereas their class uses homogeneous forms and positive-semidefinite domination on \(\mathbb R^K\). Their use of \cite{PaluckShepherdAronow2016} is a quadratic school-data empirical illustration, not a reanalysis of the original causal conclusions. \cite{Middleton2021Unifying}, \emph{Unifying Design-based Inference: On Bounding and Estimating the Variance of any Linear Estimator in any Experimental Design}, supplies the arbitrary design--estimator--bound triplet but remains matrix-quadratic. Proposition 2 and Corollary 2 in Section 3 of \cite{AronowSamii2013} use Young's inequality to construct a weakly conservative Horvitz--Thompson correction when pairwise inclusion probabilities vanish; its binary restriction lies in \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\cap\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,2}\), but that paper does not characterize the full Boolean observable-margin cone, its Pareto complete class, or the strict quartic-versus-degree-at-most-three separation. \cite{Lu2019FactorialBinary} supplies a sharp binary inclusion--exclusion correction for the \(2^2\) factorial design, while \cite{AronowGreenLee2014} supplies sharp marginal variance bounds for difference-in-means under complete randomization. \cite{ChattopadhyayImbens2025} develops imputation and contrast variance estimators, including nonquadratic procedures, but does not characterize the complete observable-function space or its Pareto frontier. \cite{AronowSamii2017Interference} fixes the design--exposure--estimand semantics and supplies inverse-probability variance estimation and local-dependence asymptotics for the school-network consumer. \cite{LiDing2017FPCLT} supplies the finite-population limit-theory benchmark; the supporting inference result derives the numerator limit from bounded independent blocks and is explicitly conditional on blockwise conservativeness and the stated denominator law of large numbers. \cite{AzrielKriegerKapelner2026}, \emph{Optimal Designs with Robust Inference for Binary Treatment Effects}, studies balanced designs and conservative CMH- and Robins-type inference under random binary potential outcomes, not unrestricted fixed binary schedules under a fixed arbitrary design.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Exact enumeration uses \(2^K\) domination inequalities, \(|\mathcal J|\) coefficients, and assignment truth tables of total size \(\sum_z2^{|O_z|}\). Independent product designs tensorize exactly, but this gives no lossless decomposition for a large connected school network. Nonnegative expected bounds also need not admit nonnegative assignmentwise tables, although the displayed quartic witness does. If \(q\) is not complement invariant, averaging a bound with its complemented version can change the objective; the odd-degree collapse then supplies no degree-three limitation, and no unsymmetric cubic-equals-quadratic claim is made.
body.honest_scope: All finite characterization, separation, and tensorization claims remain to be proved independently in the downstream derivation stage. The open school-network decomposition is exposed as \(\mathrm{oeq:school-exposure-block}\). The complete observable-function and Pareto results cover fixed binary schedules and ordinary finite randomized designs with arbitrary real probabilities on their support; rationality is imposed only by the exact primal--dual and assignment-table certificate proposition and by the displayed rational witness. The binary Aronow--Samii specialization records a published conservative Horvitz--Thompson baseline inside the quadratic cone and is not claimed as a new correction. There is no finite-sample coverage claim, no universal interval-shortening claim, no efficient general large-design algorithm, and no extension to real outcomes. Under full joint observability the theory reduces to exact variance estimability; under the proposal-specific complement-symmetry conditions and observed sets of size at most three it reduces to quadratic optimality, whereas no odd-degree collapse is claimed for unsymmetric objective weights. The Harshaw--Middleton--Savje school-data analysis is described only as a quadratic empirical illustration, not as a reanalysis of the original causal conclusions.
